title: Personal background and migration to Idaho
description: Edna Cochrane confirms her birth name, nickname, and birth date, then describes her family's move from Nebraska to Princeton, Idaho in 1912. She details traveling by train with her parents, siblings, and grandparents.

title: Family genealogy and marriage
description: Cochrane provides biographical details about her parents and their occupations, then discusses her marriage to Eugene, their wedding in Moscow, and the birth years and occupations of their four sons.

title: Education, needlework, and club memberships
description: Cochrane explains her eighth-grade education and her self-taught skills in quilting, crocheting, and collecting. She lists her extensive involvement in quilting clubs, the Rebekah Lodge, the VFW, and other community organizations.

title: Childhood, schooling, and courtship
description: Cochrane contrasts her childhood chores and school experiences with modern life, describing her preference for outdoor work. She recounts her four-year courtship with Eugene, including buggy rides and sleighing incidents, and their decision to marry.

title: Married life and family labor
description: Cochrane describes early married life caring for her husband's sisters and mother, her attitudes toward having children, and her physical labor supporting the family. She discusses her preference for field work over housework and the division of decision-making with her husband.

title: Rural life, caregiving, and reflections
description: Cochrane compares rural and urban living, explaining her husband's illness forced their move to Lewiston. She elaborates on raising nieces, nephews, and other relatives as a duty, caring for her mother, and reflecting on similarities between her life and her mother's.

title: Severe weather experiences
description: Cochrane recounts a cyclone in Nebraska when neighbors sheltered in her family's cellar and her home's roof was damaged. She describes storm protocols, compares Nebraska's cold to Idaho's climate, and contrasts wet versus dry winter conditions.
